notes.title: Nomia @ Game Devs of Color Expo 2025
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]NOMIA is featured in the GDoCExpo Direct 2025.[/p][p]Welcome to those coming from the event! The demo can be found right here:[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3610980/NOMIA_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]Please also check out the other amazing games showcasing in the [url="https://gdoc.events/Direct2025" style="button"]Direct[/url]![/p][p][/p][h2]What is this?[/h2][p]NOMIA is a story-rich tactics roguelike where you play two heroes at once.[/p][p]
Each adventurer has two decks -- a reliable Action deck and an unpredictable Gambit deck, which create wild synergies.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45555042/2b8f9ef63b46c7e9161b5911e3ec41115cdf28ce.gif"][/img]Its battle system shows enemy intents and incoming damage before you commit any moves, giving you all the information you need to execute brilliant tactics.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45555042/141c877703bab918d8a400cd4e4e675268ff9970.gif"][/img][/p][p]It is a tale of purpose and perseverance, set in a dreamlike world where adventurers battle the past to sustain the present.[/p][p][/p][h2]Why GDoCExpo?[/h2][p]I love the power of fantasy to envision a different way of being, but I am sometimes frustrated by the baggage of the genre -- a duality that made me want to try contributing my own take.[/p][p]I was born in China, and moved to Canada at a young age -- a duality I embody.[/p][p]In Chinese poetry, a [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duilian_(poetry)"]Duilian[/url] is a couplet that follows certain rules -- a duality made succinct by structure.[/p][p][/p][p]NOMIA is my attempt to make something that explores duality in its themes and mechanics, and to challenge myself to write some metrical couplets of my own.[/p][p]GDoC is a place where these dualities are celebrated, and I'm grateful to be part of its showcase.[/p][p][/p][h2]Who made this?[/h2][p]Design, art, writing, and programming are by me, Tangleworm.[/p][p]Music is by classically trained composer Will Goss.[/p][p][/p][h2]What's in the demo?[/h2][p] The demo features: [/p][list][*][p] ✨All 4 unlockable characters [/p][/*][*][p] ✨200+ cards [/p][/*][*][p] ✨100+ items [/p][/*][*][p] ✨50+ enemies [/p][/*][*][p] ✨20+ story scenes [/p][/*][*][p] ✨Save file compatibility with the full version [/p][/*][/list][p]The [b]demo will remain up indefinitely[/b], so you can play it at your own pace.[/p][p]Any feedback is welcome as I continue to build the game into the best tactics roguelike I can before its [b]October 10th Early Access launch[/b].[/p][p][/p][h3]Wishlists are sincerely appreciated![/h3][p][/p][p]Cheers, T[/p]

notes.title: Update v0.7.5
notes.notes: [p]The game now has a lore section! All the worldbuilding that would be inconvenient to convey through dialogue goes here.[/p][p]Generally, lore entries are written for knowledge that the characters would have in-universe, but wouldn't specifically talk about given the events that are happening.[/p][p]I tried to keep these from being redundant with the existing conversations, in order to enable dialogue to focus on story rather than backstory.[/p][p]In addition, you can now examine enemies in detail by clicking them in the monster library or on the run-end summary.[/p][p]Items both neutral and realm-specific can also be referenced under neutral memories list button, or by right-clicking a realm in the elemental cycle reference.[/p][p][/p][h2]CHANGELOG[/h2][p][i]v0.7.4 -> v0.7.5[/i][/p][p][/p][h3]BUG notes.title: Update v0.7.4
notes.notes: [p]The revamped tutorial is complete! It seems like folks like the game more when they get to punt something off a cliff, so now punting an enemy off a cliff is the first thing you get to do.[/p][p]Some terrain effects are also triggered on turn-end rather than on step, to encourage movement rather than staying still. To support this, damage preview now also accounts for terrain effects and lunge movement.[/p][p]I'm working on a run-modification system to support ascension-like challenge levels, but I'm still designing what those challenges should be.[/p][p]In the meantime, this system is used for assist features that make battles easier, for players who would like that.[/p][p]Next update, I'll try improving the CPU/GPU/memory performance of the game. It's been a while since I've dedicated some time to optimization.[/p][h2][/h2][p][/p][h2]CHANGELOG[/h2][p][i]v0.7.3 -> v0.7.4[/i][/p][p][/p][h3]BUG FIXES[/h3][list][*][p]Paper Hydra can now properly notes.title: Update v0.7.2
notes.notes: [p]Enemies now emphasize space control a little more, with more locked AOE attacks and terrain-generating effects in place of applying statuses.[/p][p]They also now show a damage-over-time intent distinct from the debuff intent, and several visual elements have been tweaked to reduce noise.[/p][p]Per community feedback, the party member closest to the action is now automatically selected at turn start (this can be disabled in settings if you preferred the old behaviour).[/p][p]To ease the learning curve, many of Butterfly's Momentum/Pressure/Balance generating cards now only do so on upgrade, and their original upgrades are now part of the base card. I'll be revamping the tutorial soon to make onboarding even smoother, but hopefully I can continue tweaking the card and enemy definitions to push the more complex behaviours to later in a run, when the player has had time to get used to their build.[/p][p]Next update, I'll be focusing on more visual polish and clarity![/p][p][/p][h2]CHANGELOG[/h2][p][i]v0.7.1 -> v0.7.2[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]BUG FIXES[/h2][list][*][p]Intent displays no longer temporarily disappear after failing to play a card due to unmet conditions.[/p][/*][*][p]The deselect key no longer deselects cards/units when a menu is open.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed inconsistent results with diagonal retreats.[/p][/*][*][p]Lightning Rod's Conductivity no longer activates for non-attacks.[/p][/*][*][p]Memory acquire effects now trigger again when the potency of a memory is boosted by an item.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]STORY[/h2][list][*][p]Wrote act I scene IV (not accessible in the demo currently, but it's written).[/p][/*][*][p]Hornet has new conversation portraits post-tutorial.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a serious expression portrait for each party member. notes.title: Update v0.7.0
notes.notes: [p]Hey, a new logo![/p][p]I tried tackling more of the remaining Next Fest feedback in this update.[/p][p]The camera has been overhauled with free rotation and a tactical overhead view. Visuals have been polished. The enemy roster has been expanded and tweaked for greater variety.[/p][p][/p][p]One thing that came up in playtesting was players always choosing upgrades, since they felt the safest.[/p][p]Repeated upgrades are less interesting than drafting new cards and synergizing with new memories, so let's try swapping the rarity of upgrades and memories.[/p][p]In addition, very few people were using items https://store.steampowered.com/app/3610980/NOMIA_Demo/

[h2]What is this?[/h2]

NOMIA is an isometric tactics roguelike that joins grid-based strategy with deep deckbuilding mechanics, expressed through a fantasy tale of purpose and perseverance.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45555042/2b8f9ef63b46c7e9161b5911e3ec41115cdf28ce.gif[/img]
It features a twin-deck system that enables tactical flexibility and wild synergies, as well as a turn preview that shows enemy intent and incoming damage before you commit any movement. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45555042/141c877703bab918d8a400cd4e4e675268ff9970.gif[/img]

Design, art, writing, and programming are by me, Tangleworm.
Music is by classically trained composer Will Goss!

The demo features:
[list]
[*] ✨All 4 unlockable characters
[*] ✨200+ cards
[*] ✨100+ items
[*] ✨50+ enemies
[*] ✨20+ story scenes
[*] ✨Save file compatibility with the full version

It'll also remain up indefinitely after the festival, so you can play it at your own pace.

I eagerly await your thoughts! Any feedback is welcome as I continue to build the game into the best tactics roguelike I can.

Make sure to wishlist the game, it really helps!

Cheers,
T

A few big changes this week: standard drafts now let you pick two of four cards rather than one of three, and enemies should now always spawn in the newly generated room rather than having a chance to spawn in from behind you. The former was because player decks hadn't changed as much as I would've liked by the time they reached the first boss, and the latter was because the newly generated room felt pointless if all enemies spawned outside it. This also means the party is surrounded much less often, which should hopefully open up tactical options.

On the art side, everyone's battle outfit portraits are done, and conversations are a little more fleshed out with backgrounds and cut-ins.

This version will likely be the one participating in Steam Next Fest! Wish me luck.

Since the card tutorials happened [i]after[/i] that, they never showed, and players were reading cards with no context as to how they worked.
To mitigate this, I've moved card tutorials up so they happen immediately after selecting your first unit, and made tutorial boxes contrast a bit more with the world.

notes.title: Update v0.5.5
notes.notes:
You can now preview enemy intents before committing a movement.
The lack of this information was leading to slower and more careful play, so I hope this enables more curiosity and experimentation!

In addition, any enemy that you've defeated at least once is now added to the monster library, which enables you to look directly at their cards by selecting them.

Various feedback has been implemented, such as having your party fully heal after a boss battle (rather than just 90%), adding a setting to choose between the old tile-only cursor and the new unit-sensitive cursor, and having the option to make camera rotation snap instantly to reduce motion sickness.

notes.title: Update v0.5.4
notes.notes:
The story continues!

You can now play lunge cards in all directions, not just orthogonal and diagonal.
Unfortunately, this makes past-me a liar because he wrote about his reasons for restricting lunge cards to those directions, but I found a way to make your final lunged position intuitive. Hopefully this makes longer-range lunge cards like Surging Tide more fun to play!

In response to feedback, enemies that are about to push or pull you now show a knockback preview on the target party member. Currently only Paper Hydra can ever do this (after it witnesses one of your push/pull cards), but this opens up the design space to future enemies that incorporate knockback into their standard kit.

In addition, you can now hover over a specific status icon to get a description of just that icon. No more being overwhelmed by the list of every status a unit has.
